newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan unlikely to raise interest rates soon -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan unlikely to raise interest rates soon -- MOF.

text.p: Japan is unlikely to consider raising its discount rate soon even if possible dips in the economic recovery during the April-June period turn out to be minor, a Ministry of Finance source said on Friday.
"The ministry has no intention of urging the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise its discount rate soon even if dips in the economy in the period turn out not to be so great," the source told Reuters.
"Although interest rate policy is a matter for the central bank, this is not a situation (in which the BOJ should change its interest rates)," the source added.
The finance ministry source said the economy is on a steady recovery track, with capital spending gaining strength and labour market conditions improving.

Regarding the sales tax increase on April 1, the source said the ministry is closely monitoring the effect on consumer spending as a whole, including the extent of the reaction after a rush of purchases of goods and services ahead of the tax increase.
The source said Japan would be able to achieve the government's growth forecast of 1.9 to 2.0 percent in the current fiscal year and dismissed the possibility of downside risks in the economy.
